title: Black-Box Membership Inference via Word-Level Probability Estimation
abstract: arXiv:2609.10611v1 Announce Type: cross  Abstract: Membership inference attacks (MIAs) have emerged as critical tools for auditing privacy risks in large language models (LLMs), aiming to determine whether a given text was included in a model's training corpus. However, most existing MIAs require access to per-token logits or probabilities, making them inapplicable in practice to proprietary LLMs that expose only textual continuations. To address this underexplored setting, we propose Word-level Probability MIA (WPMIA), a statistically principled MIA for strict black-box privacy auditing. WPMIA estimates word-level generation probabilities via Monte Carlo sampling with local kernel smoothing, then aggregates these estimates into a sequence-level likelihood estimator. Furthermore, WPMIA constructs the likelihood conditioned on different prefixes, thereby amplifying the distributional differences between members and non-members. translated_abstract: 成员推断攻击（MIA）已成为审计大语言模型（LLM）隐私风险的关键工具，旨在判断给定文本是否包含在模型的训练语料库中。然而，大多数现有的MIA需要访问每个token的logits或概率，这使其在实践中无法应用于仅暴露文本续写结果的专有LLM。为了解决这一尚未充分研究的场景，我们提出了词级概率MIA（WPMIA），这是一种具有统计学原理的MIA方法，适用于严格的黑盒隐私审计。WPMIA通过带局部核平滑的蒙特卡洛采样来估计词级生成概率，然后将这些估计聚合为序列级似然估计器。此外，WPMIA构建了以不同前缀为条件的似然，从而放大了成员与非成员之间的分布差异。我们在多种开源LLM上评估了WPMIA，并发现
tldr: 提出了一种名为WPMIA的黑盒成员推断攻击方法，通过蒙特卡洛采样与局部核平滑估计词级生成概率，无需访问token级logits即可对仅暴露文本输出的专有大语言模型进行隐私审计。
en_tdlr: Proposes WPMIA, a black-box membership inference attack that estimates word-level generation probabilities via Monte Carlo sampling with local kernel smoothing, enabling privacy auditing of proprietary LLMs that only expose textual continuations without requiring token-level logits.
